annotation.speech2: The x y plane with a green ellipse centered at the origin and several hyperbolas that are level curves of f equals x y. The red hyperbolas x y equals 2 and x y equals negative 2 are tangent to the ellipse at the four points 2 comma 1, negative 2 comma negative 1, negative 2 comma 1, and 2 comma negative 1. At the point 2 comma 1, a red arrow shows the gradient of f and a green arrow shows the gradient of g, pointing in the same direction.
The constraint ellipse, x squared over 8 plus y squared over 2 equals 1, drawn in green.
The branch of the level curve x y equals 2 in the first quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at the point 2 comma 1, where f attains its maximum value 2.
The branch of the level curve x y equals 2 in the third quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at the point negative 2 comma negative 1, where f also attains its maximum value 2.
The branch of the level curve x y equals negative 2 in the second quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at negative 2 comma 1, where f attains its minimum value negative 2.
The branch of the level curve x y equals negative 2 in the fourth quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at 2 comma negative 1, where f also attains its minimum value negative 2.
The level curves x y equals 1 and x y equals negative 1, drawn in gray, which cross the ellipse instead of being tangent to it: the values 1 and negative 1 are attained but are not extreme values.
The point 2 comma 1, where the absolute maximum value 2 is attained.
The gradient of f at the point 2 comma 1, drawn in red: it equals i plus 2 j.

The gradient of g at the point 2 comma 1, drawn in green: it equals one half i plus j, so the gradient of f is exactly twice the gradient of g, and lambda equals 2. The two arrows are drawn slightly apart so both are visible.
